result.title: More Memory, Better Videos? A Controlled Study of Visual Memory in Long-Video Generation
result.summary: Long-video generators increasingly retrieve past visual observations to prevent identity drift. The intuition is compelling: more access to history should make future video more consistent. But an image can be faithful to the past and wrong for the present. Does visual memory always improve the generated story? We investigate this question through VMem-Bench, a two-track diagnostic study. Track-A measures which references are selected from 92 real films (16,548 segments), before generation and without generator confounds. Track-B compares four retrieval policies with no-memory and gold-informed last-seen controls on 30 causally generated stories (2,824 segments) using a shared generator. Retrieval increases entity recall from 0.559 to 0.628-0.693 and improves similarity to past appearances, but decreases precision from 0.977 to 0.915-0.938 and forbidden-entity avoidance from 0.968 to 0.845-0.898. It can also reinforce obsolete appearances after the story changes them. Conversely, high long-gap recall can arise without memory when the prompt itself supplies the appearance; an appearance-stripping analysis exposes this confound. These results distinguish historical fidelity from current-story correctness and show why retrieval relevance or final-video consistency alone does not establish memory utility.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 VMem-Bench，用双轨诊断研究长视频生成中的视觉记忆检索：在 92 部真实影片上测量参考选择，并在共享生成器下比较四种检索策略与无记忆、给定答案的对照，考察检索对实体召回、精度和禁止实体规避的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「检索相关性或最终一致性不等于记忆有用」的结论与剥离外观线索的混淆分析，可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据是否被真正使用，以及历史保真与当前任务正确性的区分。
